relations.myth: Inheritance of the earlier birth-protective Bes-image
relations.note: Bes inherited or absorbed Aha’s frontal leonine image and protective functions.
relations.source: Middle Kingdom wands and White Chapel

relations.note: Later systematizations sometimes made the female Bes counterpart his wife.

relations.myth: Joint protection of mother and child
relations.note: They jointly protect childbirth and infancy; no secure universal marriage narrative exists.
The unnamed dwarf, probably Bes, helps rear Horus within a healing narrative.
Late objects combine Horus’s child-solar qualities with Bes’s protective form.

relations.myth: Music and celebration in Hathoric settings
relations.note: Bes serves as Hathor’s musician, celebrant and protective associate.
Bes-like musicians welcome or pacify Hathor during her return from Nubia.
Bes accompanies the returning goddess within later musical and pacifying traditions.
Bes belongs to the entourage welcoming or pacifying Tefnut’s return.

relations.myth: Pacification of the dangerous solar Eye
relations.note: Bes participates in music, intoxication and rejoicing surrounding Sekhmet’s pacification.
Bes joins the protective and musical environment surrounding Bastet’s late cult.
Mut can occupy the returning Eye’s role accompanied by Bes-like musicians.
Polymorphic Bes-images incorporate solar insignia and present him as a cosmic protector.
Late Bes pantheoi incorporate Amun’s ram horns and solar insignia.
Bes guards and celebrates the birth of Hathor’s divine child Ihy.

relations.myth: Protection of Isis and the child Horus
relations.note: Bes belongs to the late magical environment guarding Isis and her endangered child.
Bes and Tutu jointly appear as protectors who subdue hostile powers.
Later catalogues express Sopdu’s identity through the same image used for Bes.
Thoth persuades the lioness while Bes joins the related welcoming entourage.
